headline: Hot US growth and inflation data firm up December hike bets
detail: Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% pace, above forecasts, and September core PCE inflation held at 3.1% a year; markets now see roughly an 80% chance of a December rate hike. Higher rates tend to firm the dollar and weigh on metal prices.

headline: Copper falls for a third day on tech selloff and higher oil
detail: LME three-month copper slipped to about $14,320 a ton early Friday and COMEX dropped toward $6.50 a pound after weak Amazon and Intel results hit risk appetite and Brent rose on Middle East attacks. China's Yangshan import premium eased to $200 a ton but stays near a decade-plus high, which cushions the drop.

headline: Chicago ferrous scrap seen up $10–$40 a ton for November
detail: BL Duke's November outlook calls for Chicago ferrous grades to rise $10 to $40 per gross ton, while mills try to hold the increase to $10–$30. Another higher settle would lift prices for shred, HMS and busheling at area yards.

headline: Gold slips toward $4,000 and silver drops 3%
detail: Gold ended Thursday near $4,025, down about 1%, and briefly dipped under $4,000 overnight, while silver fell 3.1% to about $52.18. Rising hike odds and a firm oil price are pushing investors out of precious metals.

headline: US hot-rolled steel futures hit a four-and-a-half-year high
detail: Midwest HRC futures rose to about $1,429 a short ton early Friday, the highest since April 2022, as 50% tariffs keep imports out and give US mills pricing power. Strong steel prices keep mills hungry for prime and shredded scrap.

headline: Rio Tinto halts underground work at Oyu Tolgoi copper mine
detail: Rio paused underground operations at the giant Mongolian mine after seismic activity injured three workers, and border delays are already limiting concentrate trucks to China. Another hit to mine supply supports copper and copper scrap prices.

headline: Platinum falls under $1,450 and palladium under $1,000
detail: Platinum dropped about 3% to near $1,440 an ounce early Friday, its lowest since September 2025, and palladium slid below $1,000 on fund outflows and weak auto demand. Lower PGM prices mean lower catalytic converter payouts.

headline: Ford raises its commodity cost estimate to about $2.5 billion
detail: Ford lifted its full-year commodity cost estimate from about $2 billion, citing higher copper and steel prices, while Q3 core profit edged up to $2.7 billion and it raised the low end of its profit guidance. It said recovery from the Novelis aluminum plant fire is largely behind it.

headline: Highland Valley strikers reject Teck's offer, ready for a long strike
detail: About 1,277 workers have been out since Oct. 24 at Canada's biggest copper mine, and the union says it will reject the current offer; Teck is running at reduced capacity. A long strike tightens North American copper supply.

headline: Iron ore heads for its lowest month-end since October 2022
detail: Iron ore sits near $90.70 a ton as Chinese mills cut hot metal output and port stocks stay high. Cheap ore and soft Chinese steel keep pressure on world steel and ferrous scrap export prices.

headline: Canada not ready to sign a US trade deal before the midterms
detail: Prime Minister Carney said Ottawa won't sign yet, after the US pushed late limits on Canada's other trade deals; a framework would have halved steel and aluminum duties to 25% with quotas. With no deal, US tariffs on Canadian steel and cars are set to double Jan. 1, keeping US metal premiums high.

headline: China's October factory PMI seen flat at 50, out Saturday
detail: A Reuters poll sees the official manufacturing PMI dipping to 50 from 50.1; infrastructure investment fell 4.2% in the first nine months and Beijing has released 550 billion yuan of unused debt quota for projects. A weak reading would weigh on copper and iron ore.

headline: Indonesia says 2027 nickel ore quota will be lower
detail: Indonesia's mining director general said next year's nickel ore quota will come in below 2026's revised 290–300 million wet tons to avoid deepening the global surplus. Tighter Indonesian ore supply would support nickel and stainless scrap prices.

headline: Bank of Japan holds but says its inflation goal is met
detail: The BoJ kept its rate at 1.25% and signaled a December hike is possible; the dollar index eased to about 101.8 and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to about 4.90% as tech stocks sold off. A softer dollar gives metals a little support.

headline: Nucor: scrap costs flat, fourth quarter steady
detail: Nucor paid an average $421 per gross ton for scrap and substitutes in Q3, about the same as Q2, and sees Q4 earnings flat to slightly higher. The biggest US scrap buyer expects steady mill demand.

headline: LME aluminum seen holding $2,980–$3,100 next week
detail: LME aluminum cash fell about 1% to $3,071 a ton Thursday; SMM expects prices to consolidate as Chinese ingot stocks fall slowly and hike odds weigh. Firm aluminum keeps cast, extrusion and can prices steady.

headline: Silver could keep losing ground to gold, Metals Focus says
detail: Silver fell more than 3% Thursday, pushing the gold-to-silver ratio above 76 for the first time since December 2025, as London vault stocks rise and silver funds shed about 60 million ounces this year. More available metal points to softer silver prices.

headline: Nucor lifts spot hot-rolled coil to $1,270 a ton
detail: Nucor raised its weekly spot HRC price $15 to $1,270 per short ton, its 14th straight weekly increase. Strong mill pricing supports demand for prime and shredded scrap.

headline: Toyota's global sales and output fall for a third month
detail: Toyota reported a third straight monthly drop in worldwide sales and production. Slower auto output means less new-steel demand and fewer plant scrap flows.

headline: Builder confidence falls to its lowest since 2012
detail: The NAHB builder index fell to 29 in October and a record share of builders cut prices, with 30-year mortgages above 7%. Weak housing means less demand for copper wire, plumbing and building steel.

headline: China plans at least 2.2 trillion yuan of bond sales in November–December
detail: Central and local governments plan to raise at least 2.2 trillion yuan (about $330 billion) in the last two months of the year. More infrastructure money would help Chinese steel and copper demand.

headline: Honda warns doubled Canada tariffs would be catastrophic
detail: A Honda executive said a jump to 50% US tariffs on Canadian-built vehicles on Jan. 1 would be catastrophic for the industry. Higher tariffs could disrupt cross-border auto output and the steel and aluminum that feeds it.

headline: China copper scrap prices bounce back
detail: Chinese copper scrap grades rose about 300 yuan a ton on Oct. 27, recovering most of an Oct. 22 drop, while aluminum scrap slipped. Firm Chinese buying helps support US copper scrap export bids.

headline: Cox sees October new-vehicle sales up 7% from a year ago
detail: Cox Automotive forecasts about 1.38 million October sales and a 16.1 million annual pace, up from 15.7 million last year. Steady sales keep auto plants running and scrap flowing.

headline: Converter average slips to about $88 a unit
detail: RRCats' national average was $87.83 a converter on Oct. 28, down from about $90 two days earlier, and PGMs fell further since. Expect converter bids to stay soft.

headline: New home sales slip to a 676,000 pace in September
detail: New home sales dipped 0.6% from August and are down 5% from a year ago, with 8.4 months of supply. Slow housing means less demand for copper wire, plumbing and building steel.

headline: Canada gives Cleveland-Cliffs 15 days to reverse Stelco layoffs
detail: Canada's industry minister told Cliffs to withdraw layoff notices at its Hamilton and Nanticoke steel plants, which Cliffs blames on tariffs and cheap imports. The fight adds to the cross-border steel tariff tension.

headline: Analysts cut platinum and palladium forecasts again
detail: A Reuters survey shows analysts lowered their 2026 platinum and palladium outlooks for a third straight quarter, citing high rates and a strong dollar. That points to softer catalytic converter values.
